summary: Texas County, MO: 100-foot steel tower erected 1934, allegedly Missouri's first fire tower; staffed in 1937-38; latest dated photo found is from 2018.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mark Twain National Forest (Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek Ranger District per NHLR)

events.note: Steel tower erected in 1934; the Register calls it allegedly the first fire tower in Missouri
Lookout Kimrey, a Forest Service lookout, located in the Roby Tower in February 1937
Smoke seen from the tower on February 11, 1937; Houston Herald account printed February 25, 1937
Palmer Russell sent to work with the local towerman (November 1938); night guard and towerman assigned November 24, 1938
Houston Herald headline (article paywalled): the tower complex remains intact
Registered August 13, 2026; nominated by Audrey LaBeaume

notes_for_editor: Current condition is not verified. The newest dated evidence is a 2014 headline (the article is paywalled, so only the headline was read) and a 2018 photo credit; no 2024-26 visit or report was found. Unverified leads, not used in the story: a USAspending contract record in search results mentions tornado repair at the Roby Tower site, but that page is script-only and the bid page returned 403; a Facebook snippet says built 1937, which conflicts with 1934 from the Register and Forest Lookouts. Height 100 ft converted to 30.5 m; it is not a cab-floor measurement. Access is left unknown because no source states it. No corrections to the record.
